keys.statement: Choose extractant boiling points so regeneration takes each one overhead or at the bottom without an extra column; a heavier biocompatible extractant cut the regeneration section from three columns to two.

plain.title: Mixed extractants: choose boiling points so regeneration needs no extra column
plain.when: You regenerate a mixture of extractants after liquid-liquid extraction.
plain.do: Pick extractants whose boiling points let regeneration take each one overhead or at the bottom without an extra column.
plain.why: The boiling order fixes the regeneration sequence.
plain.check: List the boiling points of products and extractants and draw the regeneration sequence before simulating.
plain.result: A heavier biocompatible extractant cut the regeneration section from three columns to two (Grisales Díaz & Olivar Tost 2017).

decisions.mechanism: Boiling order fixes the regeneration sequence.
decisions.operation: Pick extractants with convenient boiling order.

keys.statement: Do not assume infinite extractant selectivity: real selectivities (about 300 here) carry water into the extract and need extra distillation, so use measured distribution coefficients.

plain.title: Simulated extraction needs fewer columns than reality: do not assume infinite selectivity
plain.when: An extraction model assumes the extractant takes no water, and the downstream columns come out smaller than expected.
plain.do: Use measured distribution coefficients (how a component divides between the two liquids). Real selectivities (about 300 in Grisales Díaz & Olivar Tost 2017) carry water into the extract, which then needs extra distillation.
plain.why: At finite selectivity some water is always co-extracted.
plain.check: Check the water content of the simulated extract against measured partition data.

decisions.obstacle: Simulated extraction needs fewer columns than reality.

keys.statement: For recovery from a dilute product stream, the product concentration fed to separation (set by the upstream yield) dominates the energy needed per kilogram of product.

plain.title: Dilute product stream: its concentration sets the energy per kg
plain.when: You recover a product from a dilute stream and the energy per kg is high.
plain.do: Raise the product concentration fed to separation (the upstream yield) where possible, before optimising the separation.
plain.why: Energy scales with the solvent or water handled per unit of product.
plain.check: Plot energy per kg product against feed concentration in your simulation.

decisions.obstacle: High recovery energy from dilute streams.
decisions.mechanism: Energy scales with the solvent or water handled per unit product.
decisions.operation: Raise feed concentration upstream where possible.
